brief: A workbench organizer: two storeys, bins on top, a drawer below, all edges capped.

capOpenFaces added 6 end caps across both storeys (including the top storey's cut face), and lockJoints was run. check_build reports no open-face issues and the mesh check is clear.

finish.summary: I built a two-storey workbench organizer as one column of north-half hex bases. It has a drawer on the bottom storey and a three-compartment bin on the top storey, with every open face capped and the joints bolted. check_build reports no rule issues and the mesh-collision check is clear. It came out as a half-width column because of two configurator rules. A drawer only fits on the cut face of a half base, and a base can only carry the same kind of base on top. Each cell takes a single bin, so "bins on top" is one bin split into three compartments. As a demo, a marker, a pen and a pencil stand in the compartments; they're display props, not parts. A screwdriver, a file and a hex driver wouldn't stay standing upright in the compartments, so I left them out.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
